definition: A process that moves between a fixed set of states in steps, where the probability of each possible next state depends only on the current state, not on the states before it.

A diagram of a Markov chain with one node per state and an arrow, labelled with its probability, for each possible one-step move (a loop for staying in the same state); the probabilities on the arrows leaving any one state add up to $1$.

The column $\boldsymbol{s}_0$ of probabilities (or proportions) of being in each state at the start, in the same order as the transition matrix $T$; its entries add up to $1$, and after $n$ steps the state matrix is $\boldsymbol{s}_n = T^{n}\boldsymbol{s}_0$.

A Markov chain whose transition matrix $T$ has some power $T^{k}$ with every entry strictly positive; such a chain has exactly one steady state, and the state matrix approaches it from any initial state.

A column $\boldsymbol{s}$ of non-negative entries adding up to $1$ with $T\boldsymbol{s} = \boldsymbol{s}$ for the transition matrix $T$: an eigenvector of $T$ for the eigenvalue $1$, scaled so its entries add up to $1$; for a regular Markov chain it is unique and gives the long-term probabilities.
